title: Numbers up to 1,000,000: Place Value, Reading, Writing and Comparing
seo_title: Grade 4 Numbers up to 1,000,000 Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 4)
standard_text: Read and write numbers up to 1 000 000 in numerals and in words; determine the place value of a digit in a 6-digit number, the value of a digit, and the digit of number, given its place value; compare numbers up to 1 000 000 using =, < and >.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 place value worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: read, write and compare numbers up to 1,000,000, place value and value of digits, words and expanded form. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Compare: count the digits, then compare from the left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Each digit has a place (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands) and a value (the digit times its place).
  • In 482,375 the 8 is in the ten thousands place; its value is 80,000.
  • Read big numbers in groups of three: 482 thousand, 375.
  • To compare, first count the digits. If they have the same number of digits, compare from the left.

Examples

Example

Value of 6 in 361,042

6 is in the ten thousands place

Answer: 60,000

Example

Compare 98,750 and 102,300

5 digits vs 6 digits

Answer: 98,750 < 102,300

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The digit instead of its valueThe value of 6 in 361,042 is 60,000, not 6.
Leaving out a zeroThree hundred five thousand is 305,000.
Comparing first digits of different lengthsCount the digits first.

sets.title: Place value and the value of a digit

items.q: What is the value of the digit 3 in this number?
items.e: The 3 is in the thousands place, so its value is 3 × 1,000 = 3,000. The digit is 3, but its value is 3,000.

items.q: Write this number in standard form: forty thousand, six
items.e: Before the comma, write the thousands: “forty thousand” → 40. After the comma, always write 3 digits: “six” → 006. So the number is 40,006.

items.q: What is 10 × 6,000?
items.e: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 6 thousands become 6 ten thousands. 6,000 × 10 = 60,000.

items.q: What is 10 × 400?
items.e: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 4 hundreds become 4 thousands. 400 × 10 = 4,000.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 9 ten thousands become 9 hundred thousands. 90,000 × 10 = 900,000.
Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left: 1 hundred thousand becomes 1 million. 100,000 × 10 = 1,000,000.
Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 7 ten thousands become 7 thousands. 70,000 ÷ 10 = 7,000.

items.q: What is 5,000 ÷ 10?
items.e: Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 5 thousands become 5 hundreds. 5,000 ÷ 10 = 500.
Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right: 2 hundred thousands become 2 ten thousands. 200,000 ÷ 10 = 20,000.

items.q: 800 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: Ask: 10 times what number is 800? One place to the right of the hundreds place is the tens place, so the answer is 80. Check: 10 × 80 = 800.

items.q: 30,000 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: Ask: 10 times what number is 30,000? One place to the right of the ten thousands place is the thousands place, so the answer is 3,000. Check: 10 × 3,000 = 30,000.

items.q: 500,000 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: Ask: 10 times what number is 500,000? One place to the right of the hundred thousands place is the ten thousands place, so the answer is 50,000. Check: 10 × 50,000 = 500,000.

items.q: 7,000 is 10 times as much as what number?
items.e: Ask: 10 times what number is 7,000? One place to the right of the thousands place is the hundreds place, so the answer is 700. Check: 10 × 700 = 7,000.

items.q: How many tens are in 900?
items.e: Each place is 10 times the place to its right. 900 = 90 tens, because 90 × 10 = 900.

items.q: How many thousands are in 50,000?

items.q: How many hundreds are in 7,000?

items.q: How many ten thousands are in 200,000?
items.e: Each place is 10 times the place to its right. 200,000 = 20 ten thousands, because 20 × 10,000 = 200,000.

items.q: Look at the two 3s in 33,246. The 3 on the left is worth how many times as much as the 3 on the right?
items.e: The 3 on the left is in the ten thousands place: 30,000. The 3 on the right is in the thousands place: 3,000. 30,000 = 10 × 3,000, so it is worth 10 times as much.

items.q: Which number is the greatest?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the hundreds place: 6 hundreds is more than 3 hundreds. So 78,613 > 78,316. 78,613 is the greatest.

items.q: Which number is the least?
items.e: Line up the places and compare from the left. Both have the same digits until the hundreds place: 7 hundreds is more than 5 hundreds. So 93,567 < 93,756, and 93,567 is the least.

items.q: Which comparison is true?

items.q: Three basketball games had these crowds: 26,947 fans, 29,647 fans and 24,697 fans. Which list shows the numbers from least to greatest?
